subject: Observability hooks for SDK integration and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Observability hooks for SDK integration and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks again for the time today - great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap (from today's discovery)
- FintechCo will run inference for transaction classification + risk scoring (low-latency paths for real-time decisions; batch for historical re-runs).
- Primary backends: Node.js (API) + Java (batch workers).
- P95 latency target for real-time path: ~150ms.
- Security: KMS-managed keys on your side; asking about HSM requirement for prod.

Integration asks / info we need to finalize POC
1) SDKs: which languages would you prefer example code for? (we can provide Node + Java quickstarts).
2) Auth: do you need mTLS or are API keys acceptable for an initial POC? Any KMS/HSM constraints?
3) Routing: do you need region pinning or tenant-specific routing policies?
4) Structured output / tool calling: will you use function-calling / strict JSON schemas for downstream parsers?
5) Embeddings / reranker: will you use semantic search for historical lookup (embeddings + ANN store) and a re-ranker on candidate results?
6) Observability: we propose the following hooks - please confirm these will work with your tracing/logging setup:
   - Header propagation: x-rw-trace-id (string), x-rw-span-id (optional)
   - Latency breakdown headers: x-rw-latency-ms: queue=12;compute=85;io=5
   - Logging fields in token-level logs: request_id, user_id (if provided), model, seq_len, token_count, cost_usd
   - Sample dashboards: per-route p50/p95, token-cost heatmaps, per-model error rates (link below)

Next steps
- I attached a mutual action plan and draft SOW for POC scope. Can you confirm stakeholders and whether security wants a dedicated session?
- Tech deep-dive: propose Tue Jul 20 10:00-11:00 PT (Neha + Ethan + your infra team).

Attachments: Redwood_MutualActionPlan.xlsx, MVP_SOW_draft.docx

If that looks good, we'll drop in sample SDK quickstarts and a small observability example (trace + logs) ahead of the deep-dive.

Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability hooks for SDK integration and next steps

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. Answers/notes inline below.

SDKs: Node.js + Java are perfect for us - please include a small example for our batch worker flow too.

Auth: For POC, API keys are acceptable, but for Prod we need keys stored in an HSM-backed KMS. We also prefer mutual TLS for customer-hosted/private deployments. Any KMS/HSM integration docs would be helpful.

Routing: Need region pinning (US-East for latency-sensitive traffic) and tenant-aware routing; would like a simple fallback policy if primary region is saturated.

Structured output: Yes - we rely on strict JSON schema outputs for downstream parsers; function-calling is fine as long as you can validate and return a stable schema.

Embeddings / reranker: Plan is to use embeddings for candidate generation and a cross-encoder reranker for top-5. Would like recommendations on index tech; we currently run a Faiss-based store.

Observability: OpenTelemetry-friendly is ideal. We need propagation of trace IDs into your platform (we use x-trace-id today) and prefer you accept our header or map it to x-rw-trace-id. The latency breakdown header idea looks useful - can you provide exact header names and formats so our gateway can map them?

Security team attached their security requirements (see attached FintechCo_Security_Reqs.pdf). They will likely request a short compliance session.

Tech deep-dive: Tue Jul 20 10:00 PT works for our infra and eng leads (Priya + Ilya).

Thanks - Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com | +1 206-555-0110

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability hooks for SDK integration and next steps

Thanks Marissa / Alex - tagging in a technical plan so we can be ready for the Tue deep-dive. High level plan & deliverables: 

1) SDK quickstarts (deliverable: repo + README)
   - Node.js example: sync and streaming generation; auth examples for API key and mTLS.
   - Java example: batch client with resumable checkpointing for long-running jobs.

2) Auth and KMS/HSM
   - For hosted Redwood: API keys + optional customer-managed KMS for encrypting tokens at rest.
   - For Private / on-prem: we support mutual TLS and can integrate with customer HSM via PKCS#11 or cloud KMS connectors (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM).

3) Routing and failover
   - We can expose routing policy config: region pinning + weighted fallback + model-variant fallback.
   - We'll provide a sample policy that pins to us-east and falls back to us-west with automatic variant downgrade if capacity constrained.

4) Structured output / tool calling
   - We'll showcase function-calling with JSON Schema validation; if the model deviates we'll return a structured error object with reason codes so your parsers can handle it deterministically.

5) Embeddings + reranker guidance
   - Recommend bi-encoder (for candidate retrieval) + Faiss/Annoy/HNSW for ANN. For top-k re-ranking, use a lightweight cross-encoder on the top 5-20 candidates. We'll include a sample pipeline and cost/latency estimates.

6) Observability hooks (details)
   - Trace propagation: accept x-trace-id or x-rw-trace-id; if both present we keep customer-provided x-trace-id and mirror to x-rw-trace-id.
   - Span names: model.request, model.response, kv.cache.lookup, batch.scheduler
   - Latency header: x-rw-latency-ms formatted as queue=NN;compute=NN;io=NN;total=NN
   - Detailed log fields: request_id, trace_id, user_id, model, seq_len, token_count, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, cost_usd
   - We will export OTLP spans and logs to your collector if you provide an endpoint; otherwise we can push to a temporary sandbox forwarder.

Questions for the deep-dive (so we can prepare):
- Will you provide an OTLP endpoint or prefer header-based integration only?
- Which HSM/KMS provider will be used in Prod?

Proposed deliverables before Tue: sample SDK quickstart repo, an observability example that emits a trace + x-rw-latency-ms header sample, and a one-page mapping doc for security.

Neha
